records.description: exempts affordable housing developments from 2025 to 2035 from certain electric vehicle charging installation requirements according to the 2025 standards, instead mandating compliance with the 2022 standards.

records.title: Enhanced infrastructure financing districts and community revitalization and investment areas: allocation of taxes: agricultural land exclusion.
records.description: The Williamson Act is a long-standing California program that provides tax incentives to landowners who keep their property in agricultural use. Under this bill, if a parcel is under a Williamson Act or farmland security zone contract, its taxes cannot be reallocated to an 'enhanced ingrastructure financing district' or 'community revitalization and investment area'.

records.title: Accessory Dwelling Units: ordinances.
records.description: Currently, local agencies must submit their ADU ordinances to HCD within 60 days of adoption, and HCD can review the ordinances for compliance with state standards. The bill adds a new provision that if a local agency fails to submit its ADU ordinance to HCD within 60 days or fails to respond to HCD's findings about non-compliance within 30 days, the ordinance will automatically become null/void.

records.title: Ending Street Homelessness Act.
records.description: Establishes a 7th round of the HHAP  requiring counties submit a "housing now action plan" to be eligible for funding  in order to achieve "functional zero unsheltered homelessness" (defined as housing options for at least 60% of a jurisdiction's unsheltered homeless population.) The bill requires regions to gradually expand their homeless housing capacity, targeting a 100% increase by the 2030-31 fiscal year.

records.title: Single-room occupancy units: demolition and replacement: housing assistance programs: eligibility for homeless individuals and families.
records.description: Allows cities or counties to reduce the number of replacement units required when rehabilitating/replacing single-room occupancy buildings, provided certain criteria, like converting them to affordable rental units, are met. Clarifies the definition of homelessness for eligibility in housing projects .

The Density Bonus Law mandates that cities and counties offer developers certain benefits, like density bonuses and reduced development standards, if developers dedicate a portion of their housing project to lower or very low-income households. However, this bill clarifies that these benefits do not automatically apply to transient lodging, a type of temporary accommodation, unless specified. Additionally, the bill states that cities and counties can, but are not obligated to, offer these incentives to increase floor area for nonresidential parts or specific parking areas of a housing development.

This bill would amend these acts by modifying, adding, or removing certain appropriations and implementing other changes. This bill is designed to take effect immediately as a Budget Bill and indicates the Legislature's intent to make statutory adjustments related to the 2025 Budget Act.

records.title: Residential heat pump systems: water heaters and HVAC: installations.
records.description: This bill mandates counties to implement asynchronous inspections for residential heat pump installations starting July 2027, allowing inspectors to evaluate installations without being present simultaneously with the contractor. Inspectors can require additional inspections if necessary. By July 2028, local governments are required to establish real-time online permitting for residential heat pump installations, provided the installation doesn't require major electrical or structural changes. Additionally, the bill clarifies that no permits or inspections are needed for plug-in ready window air conditioners or heat pumps meeting specific criteria.

records.title: California Environmental Quality Act: exemption: day care center: zoning.
records.description: Current law exempts specified projects from CEQA, including a project that consists exclusively of a day care center, as defined, that is not located in a residential area. This bill would instead provide that the above exemption from CEQA applies if the day care center is not located on a parcel of land zoned exclusively for residential use. The bill would additionally exempt from CEQA a project that consists exclusively of a family daycare home, as defined.

records.title: Wildfire safety: fire protection building standards: defensible space requirements: The California Wildfire Mitigation Strategic Planning Act.
records.description: Establishes a comprehensive strategic framework for wildfire risk mitigation in California. Mandates the preparation of three primary documents: a Wildfire Risk Mitigation Planning Framework (to be created every three years), a Wildfire Risk Baseline and Forecast (also updated triennially), and an annual Wildfire Mitigation Scenarios Report. Also accelerates the implementation of "zone zero" regulations, which require creating an ember-resistant zone within 5 feet of structures in high fire hazard areas, and provides grant funding to local agencies to support compliance with new requirements.

records.title: South Coast Air Quality Management District: air quality.
records.description: This bill would require the SCAQMD board to update Rule 1157 by January 1, 2027, enhancing air quality measures and data collection. It mandates facilities near sensitive receptors—like homes, schools, parks, or hospitals— to maintain certain physical barriers and storage limits for emission control. By July 1, 2027, any facility exceeding PM10 emission thresholds and located within 500 feet of a sensitive receptor must enclose open storage piles and will be subjected to monthly inspections until compliance is achieved for three consecutive months.
